memory_candidates.content: generate-context-line-counts.sh (and check-extension-docs.sh / other scripts sharing the same deploy-root-guard.sh pattern) refuse to run directly from the agent-system source store path (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/...) with a deploy-root-guard error, because '../..' resolves to a bogus repo root from that location. The sanctioned bypass for a deliberate source-store invocation is prefixing REPO_ROOT=$(pwd), e.g. `REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write` -- confirmed working this session.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh OWED-NOT-PAID fallback cost for a brand-new context file
sapience_notes.value: A genuinely new, unreferenced context file (not yet cited anywhere) triggers verify-touched.sh's OWED-NOT-PAID fallback, running the full free-cost-class suite battery (~98 suites) in addition to the normally-resolved suite set for the other touched paths -- taking several minutes rather than seconds. Confirmed live in the nvim config repo this session; this is by design, not a defect, and mirrors the same classification-branch behavior already documented for a new agent-definition file.

sapience_notes.subject: sf1-engine cross-repository obligation discharge for the sapience linked-repo write policy
sapience_notes.value: sf1-engine's integration/project-link.md section 10 names this task by its stable slug (sapience_linked_repo_write_and_capture_policy) directly in its own cross-repository register as an obligation owed back: a statement of the same write rule and sharing policy from the Claude Code side, agreeing with sf1-engine's SF-1-harness ruling by citation rather than by independent re-derivation.

sapience_notes.subject: sf1-engine ruling 7's gate does not reach a pre-verification project key field
sapience_notes.value: sf1-engine ruling 7 keeps automatic project writes attaching a verified project_cid gated OFF until two named leak paths close (a dispatched child's subsequent turns reaching the lossless feed as if typed; and Claude Code worker turns running with every hook/permission/instruction surface disabled). A plain, pre-verification 'project' key field that never sends project_cid sits entirely below that gate, so extending sapience-remember.sh with such a field does not require ruling 7's gate to be lifted.

sapience_notes.subject: rules/sapience-write-path.md's corpus figure is under-counted
sapience_notes.value: rules/sapience-write-path.md claims 14 files under the sapience extension's source store path, exactly three of which legitimately name the MCP write tools in a discussion (not prescription) sense. A live grep over those 14 surfaces found five, not three: per-repo-scoping.md, review-gate-boundary.md, EXTENSION.md, index-entries.json, and the rule file itself. EXTENSION.md's prohibition/supersession prose and index-entries.json's keywords array are legitimate discussion occurrences the rule's sanctioned-site list never named.

sapience_notes.subject: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh is a known-flaky, EXPECTED-to-fail suite
sapience_notes.value: run-all.sh's own failure classification marks test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh's 600s-per-suite timeout as (EXPECTED) rather than a NEW failure, observed twice in back-to-back verify-touched.sh runs this session with otherwise 0 NEW failures across ~120 total suite invocations. A lone EXPECTED failure for this one suite is not evidence of a regression from an unrelated change.
